Good afternoon. Here is the plan for November, and everything is already set. We are leaving on the fourth, and we are arriving in Belém in the afternoon. On the fifth we are visiting two public schools in the morning. Joice is presenting at three o'clock, in the small room. On the sixth we are meeting the German team for the last time, and we are coming back on the seventh. Please tell me if you are not coming. Thank you very much.

Hi, this is a short message about tomorrow. I am not working tomorrow morning, so we are moving our call to the afternoon. Is three o'clock good for you? The material is ready, and I am sending it tonight. Next week I am travelling to Recife, so we are not meeting on Tuesday. We are meeting on Friday instead. Please answer me soon, because I am closing the agenda today. Thank you.

Joice opens the plan for November on her computer. She sees that the group is leaving on the fourth. She writes the day of her presentation in her calendar. She asks if the room is ready for her session. She answers the coordinator and says she is coming.
